identity.name: BORANA WEAVES LIMITED
identity.industry: Synthetic Grey Fabric Weaving + Texturising — Textiles (hand-curated)

summary.oneLiner: Borana is a fully-integrated (fibre-to-fabric) synthetic grey fabric weaver in Surat — the dominant MMF hub — running at scale (~82–83% blended utilisation, near 90% ceiling) that "is currently unmatched among companies with similar product focus." Maiden post-IPO call: net-debt-free, high-return-ratio model with a clear two-year capacity-doubling runway (1,000 → 2,000 water-jet looms by Mar-28) funded largely by internal accruals + modest debt, plus a renewable-energy programme (~70–80% of power) set to protect margins as state power subsidies roll off. Q3 was a clean beat across revenue, EBITDA margin (24.3%) and PAT (+63% YoY).

thesis: Borana is a fully-integrated (fibre-to-fabric) synthetic grey fabric weaver in Surat — the dominant MMF hub — running at scale (~82–83% blended utilisation, near 90% ceiling) that "is currently unmatched among companies with similar product focus." Maiden post-IPO call: net-debt-free, high-return-ratio model with a clear two-year capacity-doubling runway (1,000 → 2,000 water-jet looms by Mar-28) funded largely by internal accruals + modest debt, plus a renewable-energy programme (~70–80% of power) set to protect margins as state power subsidies roll off. Q3 was a clean beat across revenue, EBITDA margin (24.3%) and PAT (+63% YoY).
scorecard (q3 fy26):
| Metric | Q3 FY26 | YoY | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Revenue | ₹111.36 cr | +42% | Strong order book + healthy volumes |
| EBITDA | ₹27.09 cr | +51% | Operating leverage |
| EBITDA margin | 24.32% | up | Mgmt: partly seasonal (higher-GSM winter mix) — see one-offs |
| PAT (reported) | ₹18.55 cr | +63% | Tax rate ~17.25% (15% + surcharge) |
| PAT (normalised) | ~₹18.55 cr | n/a | No exceptional items flagged; other income low at ₹1.6 cr (vs ₹3.9 cr prior qtr) |
| **VOLUME (grey fabric)** | **6.60 cr metres** (Q3) | — | 9M FY26: 16.31 cr m vs FY25 full-year 18.36 cr m |
| Realisation | ~₹16.90/sq m (Q3) | up vs ₹15.80 FY25 | Higher-GSM/winter + richer product mix |
| Utilisation | ~82–83% blended (max ~90%); Unit1 ~76–77%, Unit2 ~75% | improving | Wide 105" looms → single-width orders lower util but run 100% efficient |
| Installed capacity | 39.21 cr metres/yr; ~1,000 looms | — | +64 of 160 new 4B looms commissioned (+5 cr m annualised) |
| Net debt | Net-debt-FREE | — | Gross: ₹35 cr long-term + ₹25 cr short-term; cash ₹40–55 cr |

**One-offs / mix flags:** (a) Q3 margin lift partly *seasonal* — higher-GSM winter fabrics raise realisation; mgmt expects ~₹16+/sq m sustainable, not back to ₹15.80. (b) Other income fell to ₹1.6 cr (vs ₹3.9 cr) — prior quarter had lumpy interest-subsidy booking for Unit-3 eligibility (now booked regularly). (c) Gross-margin tailwind from Dec-25 removal of BIS restriction on Chinese yarn imports → cheaper raw material.
guidance (critical):
- **Volume / realisation:** Realisation to stay on "positive side," ~₹16+/sq m sustainable (vs ₹15.80 FY25); volume to rise with new loom commissioning.
- **Capacity ramp (new looms):** Unit 4B = ~160 new high-speed water-jet looms; 64 commissioned, **balance starting February 2026**. Adds ~5 cr metres/yr (₹60–75 cr incremental annual revenue, fully utilised by next year). Project cost ~₹35 cr.
- **Capacity DOUBLING:** 1,000 → 2,000 looms by **March 2028**; interim exit ~1,500 looms by FY27-end. Total investment ₹350–400 cr (≈₹200 cr capex + ₹50–70 cr working capital + renewables). Land available for ~700 looms; need to buy for ~300 (approvals "not a challenge").
- **Margin:** EBITDA margin to "gradually increase" QoQ as new machines complete (lower depreciation drag, falling interest cost); 25–25.5% aspirational but ~23–24% base. Q4 gross margin may beat Q3 on cheaper Chinese RM.
- **Value-add:** ~20–25% of production is value-added today; churned opportunistically with demand-supply, no fixed target. Texturised yarn ~7% of sales (kept as buffer capacity, sold as surplus, not a strategic line).
- **POY:** Backward integration into POY manufacturing only *after* capacity doubling.
demand: Polyester yarn demand "improved" and pricing "stabilized" over past months → reduced value-chain volatility, better volume visibility. PFY ~80% of India's MMF production. Borana's product is the base for dyeing/printing/finishing across apparel, home furnishings, technical textiles (tents, hospital linens, waterproof, jackets). Domestic demand easily absorbs production; export upside is *indirect* via buyers (US bedsheet demand softened; shifted to UAE/Middle East — versatile looms re-tooled accordingly).
segment (fabric / yarn):
- **Grey fabric** — core ~93% of sales; unbleached synthetic grey, sold to Surat process houses then distributed across India/world. Asset turnover ~2–3x.
- **Texturised yarn** — ~7% of sales; deliberately over-built capacity as insurance against loom downtime; surplus sold but "not part of the business to sell yarn." Not the same 2–3x asset turn.
growth / optionality:
- Capacity doubling 1,000→2,000 looms (Mar-28); interim 1,500 (FY27).
- Renewables to structurally lower power cost (largest controllable cost lever).
- Technical-textile *fabric* base (tents, hospital linens, jackets, waterproof) — Borana supplies fabric; buyers do coating. Capacity added "slowly and gradually," demand-led, no fixed capex.
- Optional forward into POY manufacturing post-doubling.
- Export optionality (indirect) — versatile water-jet looms re-configurable per destination/fabric.
margins & cost:
- RM (polyester yarn) cost "not that much fluctuating"; Dec-25 removal of BIS curb on Chinese yarn → cheaper imports, Q4 gross-margin tailwind. Mgmt confident of competing with China even at parity RM (Indian power cost similar, Chinese wages higher).
- Power/fuel/labour structurally low; bulk RM procurement aids cost + supply reliability.
- **State subsidies (rolling off):** interest subsidy ~3–4% (≈30–40% of interest cost) + power subsidy ₹2/unit (~20–22%), 5-yr per unit — Unit1 to 2026, Unit2 to 2027, Unit3 to 2028. Renewable rollout intended to offset subsidy expiry so "margin not affected at all."
capex (capacity ramp — watch):
- Unit 4B: ~₹35 cr, ~160 looms, +5 cr m/yr; 64 done, balance Feb-26.
- Doubling programme: ₹350–400 cr total (₹200 cr capex + WC + renewables) by Mar-28; ₹350 cr blended.
- **WATCH:** execution cadence of remaining ~96 looms (4B) and the larger 1,000-loom build, including land purchase for ~300 looms and phased approvals.
capital allocation (ipo proceeds / balan:
- Net-debt-free; gross debt ₹60 cr (₹35 cr LT + ₹25 cr ST); cash ₹40–55 cr. "As good as nil."
- Funding for doubling: "majorly internal accruals or maybe debt"; **no equity dilution** confirmed.
- Renewable capex ₹125 cr (₹115 cr + ₹9 cr), of which only ~₹40 cr debt, rest own funds; ~₹18–20 cr/yr power savings → ~6-yr payback.
- Non-core: ₹1 cr equity stake in **Attero Recycling** — "purely equity investment," not strategic; reiterated focus on core business only.
risks:
- **Demand/seasonality:** Q3 realisation flattered by winter higher-GSM mix — could moderate in summer.
- **Capex execution:** large multi-year loom build, land acquisition (~300 looms), approvals timing.
- **Geographic concentration:** all 4 units in Surat (mgmt defends as the MMF hub — "Manchester of synthetic fabric"; no plan to diversify).
- **Competition (Surat):** highly fragmented small/less-integrated peers — mgmt claims scale insulation but pricing discipline depends on yarn-price stability.
- **Subsidy roll-off:** power/interest subsidies expiring 2026–28; renewables must land on time (Feb-26 & May-26) to offset.
- **Export/policy:** EU GSP suspension removed Indian textile export benefit; impact indirect via buyers; RM dependence on Chinese yarn (policy-sensitive).
management tone: Confident, granular, candid (maiden call). Comfortable giving hard numbers (capex ₹35 cr, ₹350–400 cr; debt split; payback; subsidy %s; realisation/util). Repeatedly downplays competition and concentration risk ("not a challenge at all"). Some transcript garbling but substance clear.
non-obvious takeaways:
- Texturised yarn (~7%) is deliberate **redundancy capacity** (loom-downtime insurance), not a growth segment — surplus is opportunistically sold.
- Wide 105" looms create a util optic: single-width (bedsheet/shirting) orders show lower utilisation % yet run 100% efficient — utilisation % understates true output.
- The Dec-25 policy change is removal of a **BIS-certificate import restriction** on Chinese yarn (not an anti-dumping duty per se) → *cheaper* RM (gross-margin positive), a nuance vs typical import-substitution framing.
- Subsidy roll-off vs renewables is a deliberate margin-bridge: power savings (~₹20 cr/yr) sized to replace expiring power subsidy.
- ₹1 cr Attero stake is immaterial and explicitly disowned as a strategy — pre-empts any "diversification" read.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ⭐ BIS-restriction removal on Chinese yarn → cheaper RM benefits integrated Surat weavers like Borana (Q4 gross-margin tailwind).
- ⭐ Renewable-energy partners: Lakshmi Electricals (3.54 MW rooftop solar, Feb-26), Clean Max Enviro (19.79 MW solar-wind hybrid, May-26).
- ✅ Anti-dumping probe on imported textured/partially-oriented yarn supports domestic yarn/fabric pricing discipline (structural positive for the value chain).

---

Net-debt-free. Capacity 39.21 cr m / ~1,000 looms; Unit 4B 64/160 looms live (+5 cr m/yr, ₹35 cr). Guidance: double to 2,000 looms by Mar-28 (1,500 by FY27), ₹350–400 cr, no dilution; renewables ₹125 cr → ~₹20 cr/yr savings (Feb-26 & May-26); realisation ₹16+/sq m sustainable; value-add 20–25%; yarn 7%. One-offs: winter higher-GSM mix lift; other income down to ₹1.6 cr (no Unit-3 subsidy lump); Chinese-yarn BIS curb removed Dec-25 (Q4 GM tailwind).

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

- The Dec-25 policy change is removal of a **BIS-certificate import restriction** on Chinese yarn (not an anti-dumping duty per se) → *cheaper* RM (gross-margin positive), a nuance vs typical import-substitution framing.
- Subsidy roll-off vs renewables is a deliberate margin-bridge: power savings (~₹20 cr/yr) sized to replace expiring power subsidy.
- ₹1 cr Attero stake is immaterial and explicitly disowned as a strategy — pre-empts any "diversification" read.

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- ⭐ BIS-restriction removal on Chinese yarn → cheaper RM benefits integrated Surat weavers like Borana (Q4 gross-margin tailwind).
- ⭐ Renewable-energy partners: Lakshmi Electricals (3.54 MW rooftop solar, Feb-26), Clean Max Enviro (19.79 MW solar-wind hybrid, May-26).
- ✅ Anti-dumping probe on imported textured/partially-oriented yarn supports domestic yarn/fabric pricing discipline (structural positive for the value chain).

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q3 FY26 (maiden call, baseline):** Rev ₹111.36 cr (+42% YoY); EBITDA ₹27.09 cr (+51%, 24.32% margin); PAT ₹18.55 cr (+63%). Volume 6.60 cr m (9M 16.31 cr m). Util ~82–83% (max ~90%). Net-debt-free. Capacity 39.21 cr m / ~1,000 looms; Unit 4B 64/160 looms live (+5 cr m/yr, ₹35 cr). Guidance: double to 2,000 looms by Mar-28 (1,500 by FY27), ₹350–400 cr, no dilution; renewables ₹125 cr → ~₹20 cr/yr savings (Feb-26 & May-26); realisation ₹16+/sq m sustainable; value-add 20–25%; yarn 7%. One-offs: winter higher-GSM mix lift; other income down to ₹1.6 cr (no Unit-3 subsidy lump); Chinese-yarn BIS curb removed Dec-25 (Q4 GM tailwind).
